exercise2.prompt: Fixing Types: Parse a decorated amount

hiddenCases.name: a percent sign and spaces are removed
a word is not a number
a blank is not a number
the failure is caught by name

exercise2.hint: cleaned = text.strip().replace(",", "").rstrip("%"), then try: return float(cleaned) except ValueError: return None.

choices: It is a bug in Python
Text compares character by character, and "9" comes after "1"
questions.explain: Comparison stops at the first character that differs. This is why a column of numbers left as text sorts wrongly and nothing raises.
The type is right — it is a string, which int accepts — but the value is not a number, so it is a ValueError.

questions.prompt: Why does isdigit() fail as a test for "is this a number"?
choices: It is False for negative numbers and decimals
It only works on integers above zero
questions.explain: "-5".isdigit() is False, and so is "3.5".isdigit(). Trying the conversion and catching the failure covers what the test misses.

questions.prompt: Why catch ValueError by name instead of using a bare except?
choices: A bare except also hides unrelated bugs, like a misspelled variable
A bare except does not catch ValueError
questions.explain: Catch the failure you expect. Anything else should still be loud.
